text: Nib heard him. Still holding the giant blade on his crossed knives, he answers his old commander: he'll end it.
But the voice is gone. The red floods back into the hole, like a fever returning.
The knight leans its whole weight on the sword and drives Nib down onto one knee.
So Jaeha uses Carry, moving a summon's damage into his own body. Give him half.
Half the knight's weight lands on Jaeha's shoulders instead, and his nose starts bleeding again.
Nib feels the load ease and glances back, startled.
Yerin slides in behind Jaeha with glowing hands, still shaking. Keep going. She'll keep him on his feet.
Through Link, he looks out of Nib's eyes into the knight's face. There: a crack in the rim of the hole.
One thin crack, glowing brighter red than the rest.
Nib sees it too, and he is steady now. Do it. He asked them to.
Jaeha isn't polite at all anymore. Then they do it together. On his call.
The knight tears its sword free and winds up one last sweep. The left shoulder drops. Wait for it.
Now! The sweep passes underneath, and Nib springs off the knight's own forearm and drives both knives into the crack.
The knight sinks to its knees. Boss defeated: a hushed knight-commander, grade B-plus, registered as C. The red lamp was right.
Then two windows. Harvest the core, worth an estimated four hundred million won. Or release.
Yerin can only whisper the number.
For one moment, Jaeha sees home. The rent is due Friday, and his sister Seoa's school trip isn't paid.
The cyan glow sits in his tired eyes.
His finger hovers between the two. Wait. What does release actually do?
The answer: the remains return to their own.
Nib stands before his old commander, small, head bowed.
Jaeha looks past the windows at Nib's back.
And he presses release.
Nib spins round. Four hundred million, and he gave it up?
Jaeha shrugs, embarrassed. He was Nib's commander. He should go home. Privately, Jaeha knows Seoa is going to kill him.
The knight dissolves into rising light, its ash lifting like embers.
For one moment there's a real face in the helm, an old soldier's, scarred, with kind eyes. Nib. You found an Operator.
Go first for him, he says, and make sure he comes back.
Nib gives the old salute, fist over his heart, tears running below the mask. Yes, commander.
Then the knight is gone, and a column of ash drifts up through the light.
The modern chains crumble to dust. All but one link.
Jaeha picks it up. Factory steel, stamped with a small mark. Someone on this side of the gates chained him here.
Its sword stays behind: over two metres of dark iron, the crossguard shaped like a wall with nine towers.
It slides into a slit in the air. Item: the Ninth Wall Blade. Strength required, ninety. Jaeha's strength: seven.
He tries to draw it, and its weight slams the point into the floor and drags him down with it.
He strains with both hands and one boot. Nothing. That was the commander's sword, Nib says. Try not to drop it again.
Pinned flat under his new sword, Jaeha begs the system to put it back.
Then the rewards pour in. Operator level one to three. Link and Carry, level two. Route Alignment, zero to thirty percent.
And a title: The One Who Went Back.
His status window: class, Operator. Shown to others as an F-rank summoner. Summons: one of one.
Jaeha is baffled. What is an Operator?
Nib, deadpan: you are, apparently.
Then a cold warning. Operator authority cannot be transferred. If the Operator is forced, the protocol ends.
And another: the gate is closing in thirty seconds. The hall starts breaking into flakes of light.
Nib kicks the bolted door, and the bolt outside snaps.
Then he stands aside with one palm out, completely deadpan. You first. Now? The whole gate is collapsing!
They sprint up the corridor as it crumbles behind them. Four seconds.
And they dive out into the subway pit as the gate snaps shut behind them.
Gate 0912, eleven thirty-one at night. The street is full of rescue trucks and flashing lights.
Choi Dongmin, thirty-four, of the Gate Rescue Corps, wraps Jaeha in a foil blanket. An F-rank and a rookie walked out of a gate that killed four B-ranks? He'll need more coffee.
He points his cup at Nib, wrapped in foil like a tiny burrito. And the little guy? His husk, sir. A very unusual husk.
Nib eyes the steaming coffee by his face. You first.
Choi slowly lowers the cup. Did his husk just talk to him?
Jaeha smiles very politely, sweating, while Nib freezes like a doll. It makes sounds when it's tired, sir.
Then the billboard across the street lights up: Black Hound's live press conference. Four hunters dead. Trap-tester missing.
Mok, solemn at a podium: their trap-tester set off a hidden boss, and four of their hunters died.
Kang Jaeha is presumed dead. One corner of Mok's mouth isn't quite grave.
Yerin covers her mouth. Choi, coffee frozen halfway, mentions that Jaeha is presumed dead, by the way.
Jaeha isn't smiling now. Presumed dead? Then he'd better go to his own funeral.
